caption: The drawing depicts three fireplace tools arranged vertically and evenly spaced against a beige background, all with detailed shading and outlined by a thin rectangular border. From left to right, the first object is a pair of tongs with black elongated handles and a decorative gold handle in a turned cylindrical shape at the top, ending in rounded gripping ends. The middle object is a two-pronged fork with similarly shaped and colored handles; the gold decorative top is above a circular element with a horizontal rod connecting the two sides, and the prongs are parallel and black. The third object on the right is a shovel with a broad, flat, black scoop at the end of a long, straight black shaft that transitions to gold at the upper section, also topped by the same turned cylindrical gold handle design as the others. Below the tools are two horizontal scale bars marked for measurement; the one on the left is more detailed, while the one under the fork is simpler. In the bottom left corner, the name "HANS KORSCH" appears in capital letters. The drawing uses mainly black and gold tones with subtle shadow, and all tools have similarly styled, elaborate handles.
title: Fire Tongs and Shovel
